We'll make another version of M5LAB1 – Choose Your Own Adventure, but this time it's a cooking game!

The player is a chef opening a restaurant. Customers arrive hungry, and the player must decide what to cook and how to prepare it. Make the right decisions, and the restaurant becomes successful. Make the wrong decisions, and the customers might never come back!

M5LAB1 – Cooking Chaos: The Restaurant Adventure

respawn.outlookindia.com

Complete C++ Code

This version uses four main menu options, input validation, and three separate story functions. It meets both parts of your assignment.

C++

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

// Function prototypes
void main_menu();
void cook_pizza();
void cook_burger();
void cook_pasta();

int main()
{
    cout << "===================================" << endl;
    cout << "     COOKING CHAOS RESTAURANT      " << endl;
    cout << "===================================" << endl;

    cout << "\nWelcome to your new restaurant!" << endl;
    cout << "You are the head chef." << endl;
    cout << "Hungry customers are waiting!" << endl;
    cout << "Can you become a master chef?" << endl;

    main_menu();

    return 0;
}

// Main menu
void main_menu()
{
    int choice = 0;

    while (choice < 1 || choice > 4)
    {
        cout << "\nWhat would you like to cook?" << endl;
        cout << "1. Make a pizza" << endl;
        cout << "2. Cook a burger" << endl;
        cout << "3. Prepare pasta" << endl;
        cout << "4. Close the restaurant" << endl;
        cout << "Enter your choice: ";

        if (!(cin >> choice))
        {
            cin.clear();
            cin.ignore(10000, '\n');
            choice = 0;
        }

        if (choice < 1 || choice > 4)
        {
            cout << "Invalid choice! Try again." << endl;
        }
    }

    if (choice == 1)
    {
        cook_pizza();
    }
    else if (choice == 2)
    {
        cook_burger();
    }
    else if (choice == 3)
    {
        cook_pasta();
    }
    else
    {
        cout << "\nRestaurant closed!" << endl;
        cout << "Thanks for playing!" << endl;
    }
}

// Story branch 1 - Pizza
void cook_pizza()
{
    int choice = 0;

    cout << "\nA customer orders a pizza!" << endl;
    cout << "What topping will you use?" << endl;

    while (choice < 1 || choice > 2)
    {
        cout << "1. Pepperoni" << endl;
        cout << "2. Pineapple" << endl;
        cout << "Enter your choice: ";

        if (!(cin >> choice))
        {
            cin.clear();
            cin.ignore(10000, '\n');
            choice = 0;
        }

        if (choice < 1 || choice > 2)
        {
            cout << "Invalid choice! Try again." << endl;
        }
    }

    if (choice == 1)
    {
        cout << "\nThe customer loves the pepperoni!" << endl;
        cout << "You earn a five-star review!" << endl;
    }
    else
    {
        cout << "\nThe customer sees pineapple!" << endl;
        cout << "They start a debate about pizza!" << endl;
        cout << "At least the pizza tastes good!" << endl;
    }

    cout << "\nTHE END!" << endl;
}

// Story branch 2 - Burger

M5LAB2 - Complete a Program

In previous labs, I've built a program and asked you to follow along.

This time I've built part of a program, but it's not finished. Your task is to complete the program by writing the missing functions.

There are more than one syntax errors (typos) in the existing code, so you'll need to fix those as well. (Getting stuck fixing someone else's code is definitely something that happens in programming.)

The partially completed file: AreaRectangle.cpp If you have trouble opening the file in a text editor (Notepad will work), change the extension to .txt.

Here are the program specifications.

The program will ask the user to enter the width and length of a rectangle. It will then calculate the area. Finally it will display all three values in well formatted output.

The program will contain the following functions as well as main().

getLength - Asks the user to enter a rectangle's length, and return that value as a double.

getWidth - Asks the user to enter a rectangle's width, and return that value as a double.

getArea - This function should take two arguments, length and width. It will calculate the area and return that value as a double.

displayData - This function should take three arguments, length, width, and area. It will then display these values as well formatted output. ("Well formatted" is subjective, at minimum each value should be clearly labeled. The Apple Orchard program from Module One is an example of the type of output format you might use.)

TOTALLY OPTIONAL ADDON

Use a function to get input once!

M5LAB2 – Complete a Program: Rectangle Area Calculator

For this assignment, we're going to create a straightforward C++ Rectangle Area Calculator.

Unlike M5LAB1, where we created a cooking adventure, this assignment focuses on using functions to perform specific tasks.

Your instructor requires four functions:

Function

Purpose

Return type

getLength()

Ask for the rectangle's length

double

getWidth()

Ask for the rectangle's width

double

getArea()

Multiply length × width

double

displayData()

Display length, width, and area

void

The formula is:

Area=Length×Width\text{Area}=\text{Length}\times\text{Width}Area=Length×Width

We'll keep the program simple, use clearly labeled output, and organize the functions exactly as your instructor requested.

Complete C++ program

Copy this into AreaRectangle.cpp in GitHub Codespaces.

C++

#include <iostream>
#include <iomanip>
using namespace std;

// Function prototypes
double getLength();
double getWidth();
double getArea(double length, double width);
void displayData(double length, double width, double area);

int main()
{
    double length;
    double width;
    double area;

    cout << "================================" << endl;
    cout << "    RECTANGLE AREA CALCULATOR   " << endl;
    cout << "================================" << endl;

    // Get the rectangle measurements
    length = getLength();
    width = getWidth();

    // Calculate the area
    area = getArea(length, width);

    // Display the results
    displayData(length, width, area);

    return 0;
}

// Get the rectangle length
double getLength()
{
    double length;

    cout << "\nEnter the rectangle length: ";
    cin >> length;

    return length;
}

// Get the rectangle width
double getWidth()
{
    double width;

    cout << "Enter the rectangle width: ";
    cin >> width;

    return width;
}

// Calculate the rectangle area
double getArea(double length, double width)
{
    double area;

    area = length * width;

    return area;
}

// Display the rectangle measurements
void displayData(double length, double width, double area)
{
    cout << fixed << setprecision(2);

    cout << "\n================================" << endl;
    cout << "       RECTANGLE RESULTS        " << endl;
    cout << "================================" << endl;

    cout << "Length: " << length << endl;
    cout << "Width:  " << width << endl;
    cout << "Area:   " << area << endl;

    cout << "================================" << endl;
}

Example output

If you enter a length of 10 and a width of 5, the program should display:

TERMINAL OUTPUT

Plain text
================================ RECTANGLE AREA CALCULATOR ================================ Enter the rectangle length: 10 Enter the rectangle width: 5 ================================ RECTANGLE RESULTS ================================ Length: 10.00 Width: 5.00 Area: 50.00 ================================

Step-by-step submission instructions

  1. Open your M5LAB2 assignment in GitHub Codespaces.

  2. Locate AreaRectangle.cpp.

  3. Replace the code with the completed version above.

  4. Save the file.

  5. Compile and run the program.

  6. Test with a length of 10 and width of 5. Your answer should be 50.00.

  7. Commit and push your changes to GitHub.

The program fulfills all four required functions, uses double values, and formats the results to two decimal places.
